text:
maria (support): Customer ACME reports a sudden latency jump and ~3x egress/billing increase since 09:12 UTC. They also saw sporadic 401s for signed keys. Ticket: #7892.

sasha (csm): They noticed requests routing to ap-southeast even though their customer region is us-west. Latency tail is ~900ms.

maria (support): Repro steps from customer: curl to our API endpoint with their API key returns X-Region: ap-southeast and slower RC. They said policy changes were made this morning via console.

jonathan (eng): Hmm. Can you paste the effective failover policy we resolved for that org? Any recent deploys?

maria (support): Attaching policy snippet they pasted in chat: ```json
{"priority":["ap-southeast","us-west"],"weights":{"ap-southeast":0.7,"us-west":0.3},"sticky":true,"ttl":3600}
``` They claim expected priority was us-west first.

kevin (infra): That policy looks inverted — priority array is [ap-southeast, us-west]. If the UI shows the other order maybe the backend parsed it lexicographically on string keys during migration. Also noticed weights are floats.

jonathan (eng): Also, sticky:true with ttl 3600 will keep sessions stuck to the first seen region. If the order is inverted, new sessions will prefer ap-southeast and persist for an hour -> cross-region egress and billing.

maria (support): Customer says they edited via Console -> Save -> Confirm. Console returned success. No warning.

jonathan (eng): Steps to reproduce I want to try: 1) apply the policy exactly as pasted; 2) crunch a few synthetic requests from a us-west IP; 3) check selection header X-Selected-Region and cookie.

kevin (infra): Quick check: I grepped policy commit history and found a migration script from earlier today that serializes priority array as comma-joined string for storage and the parser in the routing service splits and reverses on empty trailing comma. In one code path it reversed order. Suspect that.

maria (support): Customer also sent logs: ```
[09:15:03] req=abcd region=ap-southeast selected=ap-southeast cookie=stky=1
[09:15:04] req=abce region=us-west selected=ap-southeast ttl_remain=3598
[09:20:00] 401 api_key=acct-123 origin=us-west selected=ap-southeast
```

sasha (csm): 401s could be because signed key validation hits a different auth cluster region — our signed-key service expects requests from us-west for this customer. Cross-region routing hitting ap-southeast auth cluster returns 401.

jonathan (eng): Okay action items: 1) kevin, pin down the migration parser bug and rollback the code path to preserve array order (hotfix). 2) me, add validation in Console that shows effective region order before commit and Warn if sticky=true and first priority != customer's home region. 3) maria/sasha: ask customer to temporarily set sticky=false or set explicit priority to force us-west until we patch.

kevin (infra): I can hotfix the parser and push a canary within 30 min. Will also add a gate in the migration job to preserve original array indices.

maria (support): For mitigation with customer: suggested curl to force region via header X-Preferred-Region: us-west and a temporary policy change. Provided these commands: ```bash
# quick test forcing region header
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ${KEY}" -H "X-Preferred-Region: us-west" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -I
```

sasha (csm): Also opened billing review with finance — flagged potential egress overage while root cause is active.

jonathan (eng): After hotfix, we'll run a small diff test across 1000 requests to ensure selection flips back. maria, please coordinate rollback window.

gatekeeper-bot: deploy job #4321 started by kevin — canary routing-service:sha@a1b2c3.

kevin (infra): Canary up. Early telemetry shows new parses preserve original priority ordering. Rolling to 10% traffic.

maria (support): Customer confirmed initial drop in ap-southeast hits after we applied header workaround, will wait for hotfix. Keeping ticket open.

jonathan (eng): Postmortem items: - harden policy serialization/parser - add console warning for sticky+remote-first combos - add E2E test that simulates migration path.

sasha (csm): Customer is relieved but wants a formal RCA and notes about billing credit. I'll prepare comms when RCAs ready.

maria (support): Thanks team. I'll update ticket #7892 and loop in billing after root cause confirmed. :thumbsup:
